messages:
pagerbot: 🔔 INCIDENT P0 - Service-proxy unusual token issuance spike detected. Alert id: A-2026-171999.  traffic: ~4500 token-create/sec from 82.14.66.0/29 and 203.0.113.0/24. Possible automated replay or compromised CI key. Autopage to #incidents & on-call.

alice.ops: oncall, please ack and triage. tagging @ben.oncall. I see a correlated increase in 502s for downstream auth-gateway.

ben.oncall: ack — I'm on it. Beginning triage. First question: customer impact? any data exfil flags?

carla-sre: visibility: upstream queueing spike → some request latencies hit 2.5s, retries increased. No large-scale 5xx for product APIs yet, but auth service error rate up 8x. I pulled sample logs: many requests using service token pattern svc-proxy-* with identical user-agent: "curl/7.79.1".

ben.oncall: thanks. @david-sec can you weigh in on rotation plan? recommend immediate revoke of impacted service tokens and short-term WAF/ACL blocks?

david-sec: recommend triage steps: 1) block the offending CIDRs at edge WAF 2) throttle token-create endpoint to authenticated clients only for now 3) rotate service tokens created in the last 24h for any svc-* principal 4) preserve logs for forensics. I’m standing by to execute rotations.

eve-support: support update: two enterprise customers reported auth flakiness. Opening incident tickets with subject "Auth instability" and linking to this thread.

carla-sre: mitigation action 1: adding WAF deny rules for 82.14.66.0/29 and 203.0.113.0/24 now (rule id tmp-block-171999). Deploying with zero-downtime commit via deploy-bot.

deploy-bot: started rollout for waf/tmp-block-171999 → 3 edge nodes. status: rolling (1/3 applied).

ben.oncall: execute rotation for high-risk svc tokens. We should scope to tokens issued in last 24h with pattern svc-proxy-*. What is the admin API call?

david-sec: use internal revoke endpoint (limited admin token required). Example:```bash
curl -X POST "https://admin.redwood.internal/v1/keys/revoke" \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"identifiers": ["svc-proxy-*"], "issued_since":"2026-03-18T00:00:00Z"}'
```
Note: will cause immediate failure for valid services using those keys. We should coordinate safe restarts or issue rotated keys to critical services first.

alice.ops: we need a canary rotation plan: 1) revoke a non-customer-critical svc-proxy key to validate rollback 2) rotate critical keys via staging secret push + restart 3) inform customers if their token belongs to affected svc-acct.

ben.oncall: agreed. I'll run the canary on svc-proxy-canary. Carla — can you confirm downstream retry/backoff tolerance for that service?

carla-sre: svc-proxy-canary has 5s retry backoff, should be safe. Starting canary revoke now.

deploy-bot: revoke call queued: admin/keys/revoke (canary) -> status: success. canary observed: token rejected, failover to cached path OK, no customer impact.

ben.oncall: canary looks good. Proceeding to bulk rotation for keys issued last 24h for svc-proxy-*. Executing in 10m window. @david-sec please standby to lock down IAM if we see collateral failures.

david-sec: standing by. Also requesting forensic snapshot: capture auth-gateway headers, raw token material, and origin IPs for all token-create events between 1719991200-1719995555. Use runbook: https://wiki.redwood/incident/runbooks/auth-spike for preserved evidence steps.

carla-sre: implemented temp-rate-limit on /v1/token/create from 1000rps -> 200rps for unauthenticated endpoints. Rule id rate-tmp-171999.

eve-support: notifying top 10 affected customers: ticket created + status page draft. No PII confirmed exposed so far.

ben.oncall: starting bulk revoke now. Will post updates every 2 minutes.

deploy-bot: admin/keys/revoke (bulk svc-proxy-24h) -> applied to 73 tokens.

carla-sre: monitoring: token-create rate dropped to baseline after WAF + rate limit. Auth error rate returning to normal. No signs of exfil pattern in request paths.

david-sec: rotation complete for affected keys. Generating ensure script for new keys rollout. Also starting background job to create new ephemeral service tokens with 1h TTL for higher-risk services.

ben.oncall: good job. Please confirm whether any customer-facing systems fell below SLA.

eve-support: short blip for two customers (10-12 minutes) where API calls returned transient auth failures due to rotation; both notified and tickets linked.

david-sec: recommending follow-ups: 1) audit CI/CD secrets to find possible leaks 2) expand monitoring on token creation rate and unusual user-agents 3) legal notified if any confirmed exfil. I've created infra ticket SEC-1721 for CI secret audit.

alice.ops: handoff plan: ben to coordinate postmortem + timeline. carla to own metrics dashboard updates. david to own security follow-up. eve to own customer communications. We'll run a short bridge at 1730 UTC to collect notes.

ben.oncall: taking postmortem lead. I'll draft timeline and include exact IP blocks, token ids rotated, and support impact. Expected SLO impact: <0.1% customers degraded.

carla-sre: saving full log snapshot to s3://redwood-incidents/1719995555-auth-spike.tar.gz and tagging for forensics.

david-sec: all rotations documented in internal key-rotation log. Recommend rotating any CI tokens discovered by SEC-1721 within 48h.

eve-support: status update posted to status.redwood.com: "Investigating - elevated auth traffic; mitigations applied; customer impact minimal".

ben.oncall: closing on-call window for immediate triage. If any new anomalous traffic appears, page oncall-escalation. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

pagerbot: incident state changed -> mitigated. Incident ticket A-2026-171999 set to postmortem_pending.

alice.ops: adding timeline note and scheduling postmortem meeting. Thanks everyone."
